mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from t-1w to t-0w will continue to pull more weekday trips into the city, lifting retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last-4-week mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain above their t-1w levels for at least two of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL falls below 8 points above baseline, the implied shift away from staying home releases discretionary outing time, causing RETAIL_REC to increase within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines for two consecutive weeks after RESIDENTIAL drops below 8 and remains there.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES creates a commuting-plus-lunch pattern that increases incidental shopping and dining visits, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, falling TRANSIT is a leading sign of suppressed nonessential trips, so RETAIL_REC will decline over the next month even if grocery mobility remains stable.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -22 and keeps declining week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays above its recent average despite TRANSIT dropping below -22 for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A contemporaneous improvement in PARKS and RETAIL_REC indicates warmer-weather or holiday outing spillovers; if PARKS keeps rebounding, retail mobility should rise over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks while PARKS rises from its t-0w level.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both remain elevated, households concentrate trips on necessities and at-home activity, which suppresses discretionary retail visits over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above -11 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the week after both GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL remain above the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained narrowing of the gap between WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL signals resumption of out-of-home routines; if that gap shrinks further, retail mobility should improve over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its recent average even as WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls for at least three of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovers while PARKS do not, the mobility mix shifts toward structured urban movement rather than leisure substitution, producing a short-run gain in RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -20 while PARKS remain below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks after TRANSIT rises above -20 while PARKS stay below -25.
